common_ground: Timing: mid/late February through April, peak in March
Cause: agricultural crop-residue burning (Thailand + Laos/Myanmar/Cambodia) plus forest fires, worsened by valley geography trapping smoke
Generic coping tactics: N95 masks, HEPA air purifiers, limiting outdoor time, live AQI-app monitoring (IQAir/Aqicn.org)
Travel-planning framing: should-you-visit, alternative months/regions, FAQ block

gap.description: Every ranking result treats burning season as a pure tourism/health-logistics problem (mask up, buy a purifier, maybe reschedule your trip). None address the specific, high-intent question Wildcat's actual audience has: 'I'm flying in to train Muay Thai for weeks — can I still train hard, and how does a camp handle the smoke?' No competitor discusses adjusting training intensity/schedule around AQI, indoor vs outdoor session planning, gym air filtration, or how a resident who trains daily actually lives through it season to season.

weakness: Authorship is either an anonymous 'team' byline (backpackthailand, thailandfaq) or a generalist local blogger/accommodation business (cnxlocal, adahouse) — none is someone who trains or coaches daily outdoors in Chiang Mai, which is a stronger E-E-A-T angle for a YMYL health topic tied to physical exertion

Coping-strategy sections are copy-paste generic (mask, purifier, stay indoors) across all 3 fetched articles, with no sport-specific nuance (e.g. safe AQI thresholds for cardio, why early-morning sessions differ from midday, how enclosed/covered training spaces compare to fully open-air gyms)

None distinguish the shoulder months clearly for a training-trip planner — Nov-Jan (high season, clean air) vs Feb (transition) vs March (peak, real disruption) vs April (Songkran + tail-end smoke) — the framing stays tourist-generic, not booking-decision-specific
recommended_angle: Write it as Meaw's own on-the-ground playbook for burning season at a camp that trains outdoors: what changes at Wildcat when AQI spikes (indoor/covered sessions, timing shifts to clean-air hours, gear and gym-side precautions), plus an honest month-by-month verdict for anyone planning a training trip (Nov-Jan safe bet, March the real risk window) — the angle no travel blog or clinic page owns because none of them actually run daily outdoor training through it.
